prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1379; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- Records show the same major damage from an earlier, unreported accident; it is now claimed as new.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: On arrival at the intersection in Sugar Land, Texas, I found a rear-end collision between a sedan operated by Driver 1 and an SUV operated by Driver 2. Passenger was seated in the front passenger seat of Driver 1's vehicle. Driver 2 stated that the sedan stopped abruptly at the signal and that the SUV struck it from behind. Two independent witnesses and photographs taken at the scene support that account. Driver 1 reported pain in the right shoulder and was transported by EMS for evaluation. The nature of the injury and the force of the impact appear consistent with each other. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the sedan. Records retrieved during follow-up show that the sedan had sustained similar major front-end damage in an earlier incident that was never reported to police or the insurer. It is not clear from the physical evidence whether all of the current damage resulted from this collision. A supplemental inspection has been requested to determine the extent of the prior damage.
